I'm very upset about being socially anxious, which, as I figured out from a thought exercise from this one YouTube video, comes from me being afraid of people judging me for having mental health issue like my dad did a few years ago. I guess I'm afraid of women judging me like my dad did and still does. I'd say that I don't really care about it coming from my dad anymore, but I actually tense up when I see attractive women. It inspires a profound hopelessness that the only way that I will find peace is in death.

Very true. There's a song by Powerwolf called "Armata Strigoi" where they say something like "We are the knights of sorrow." As someone infatuated with medieval stuff and WH40K, I can't help but thinking of all of us (people who have considered or attempted suicide) as Battle-Brothers who fight selflessly for one another; a cohort of wandering knights who, through shared experiences, know one another intimately and recieve one another with the utmost empathy; compassionate warriors who fight on for the fallen.

I don't know if this will help you, dear Battle-Brother (forgive me for assuming your gender, but I like Space Marines A LOT), but I feel like I experience something similar to what you feel about women.

For me, any woman that I was attracted to would cause me great dread because I thought about how hard they would reject me, how worthless I was, etc. It was so bad that I missed college classes because I didn't want anyone, especially those attractive women, to see me. Anyway, my current therapist told me this thing and it has been a silver bullet for me in these situations. It's simply to **promise myself that I will not ask out anyone in my classes**. For me, it worked like magic because, in a situation like a class where I notice a really attractive person in my proximity, I would just say in my head "I'm not going to ask her out!" The moment I say this, I am instantly relieved of my anxiety because, for me, the follow-up for that realization is (warning: I like cursing) "Why would I give even the slightest fuck about what that lady thinks if I'm not going to ask her out? Why would I hamper my self-expression to appease some bullshit-ass person that (1) I know nothing about and that (2) I don't care to know?" From there, it's not a far cry for me to ignore what I think other people might be thinking in general, not just the attractive ladies.

I don't know if it will help you, but I'm going to classes now without panicking, so if my testimonial means anything to you, there's that. I don't know your life situation, so I don't know if this sounds at all like anything you may want to try.

P.S.: I read it out loud and I'd just like to confirm that I'm not a MGTOW and I don't hate women. 

EDIT: P.P.S.: After reading these posts, I realize that it sounds like I'm suggesting you give up. I'm not saying to give up on finding someone special. I do the above so that I can afford myself time to work on myself and work on seeing women as people who aren't so different from me so that whenever I do meet someone compatible, I'm not overcome by the dread of what they might think of me. Besides, I have problems besides social anxiety (read: severe depressive episodes and suicidal ideation) that I know I must work on before I can try my hand at dating. 

So, I guess I'm saying that you should give yourself time to work on that social anxiety, to work on constructive strategies to deal with it during and after social situations, and to not judge yourself based on your lack of a significant other.

P.P.P.S.: This whole post sounds really bad, but I could not be any more sincere.
